killings.feud_name: Killing of Þorvaldur Ósvífsson (Hallgerður's first marriage)
killings.evidence: ch.11: "Eg vissi eigi," segir hann, "en þó skal eg þessa hefna."
killings.note: Revenge word used, but for the slap given to Hallgerður, not for a killing; so no avenges fields.

killings.feud_name: Glúmur–Þjóstólfur killings (Hallgerður's second marriage)
killings.evidence: ch.17: Glúmur mælti: "Eg skal taka hæðiyrði af þér þar sem þú ert þræll fastur á fótum." ... Þá reiddist Glúmur og hjó til Þjóstólfs
killings.settled_after: yes (ch.17, gifts to Þórarinn instead of compensation)
killings.note: Quarrel; Glúmur struck first, so partly self-defence. Glúmur had slapped Hallgerður (ch.16), who forbade Þjóstólfur to avenge it.

killings.feud_name: Glúmur–Þjóstólfur killings (Hallgerður's second marriage)
killings.avenger_relation: uncle of Glúmur's wife Hallgerður (ch.13, ch.17)
killings.evidence: ch.17: "Eigi veldur hún þessu þá," segir Hrútur og brá sverðinu. Höskuldur: "þegar Hrútur vissi þá drap hann Þjóstólf."
killings.note: Þjóstólfur struck first after Hrútur drew his sword; no revenge word, but Hrútur acts at once on news of Glúmur's death and Höskuldur thanks him.

killings.feud_name: Ásgrímur kills his foster-brother Gaukur
killings.evidence: ch.26: "Þar varð illa með þeim Ásgrími því að Ásgrímur varð banamaður Gauks."
killings.note: Aside only; killed his own foster-brother.

killings.feud_name: Hallgerður–Bergþóra feud (servant killings)
killings.evidence: ch.36: "Svo mun Bergþóra til ætla," segir Hallgerður, "að ræna mig mörgu en því skal eg ráða að hann höggvi eigi oftar."
killings.note: Root cause is the seating quarrel at Bergþórshvoll (ch.35); pretext is Svartur cutting wood in Gunnar's forest (property).

killings.feud_name: Hallgerður–Bergþóra feud (servant killings)
killings.evidence: ch.37: "nú skalt þú vega hann í dag ef þú vilt minn vilja gera." ... "þrælsgjöld þau er vér tókum við fyrra sumar ... munu nú koma fyrir Kol."
killings.settled_after: yes (ch.37, settled with the thrall-price paid for Svartur)
killings.note: Bergþóra commissions the killing; the compensation for Svartur is turned round as compensation for Kolur.

killings.feud_name: Hallgerður–Bergþóra feud (servant killings)
killings.avenger_relation: Hallgerður's kinsman, Kolur's successor as overseer at Hlíðarendi (ch.38)
killings.evidence: ch.37: "Hallgerði var sagt víg Kols og ummæli Atla. Hún kvaðst launa skyldu Atla."
killings.note: Revenge is Hallgerður's; Brynjólfur is her instrument.

killings.feud_name: Hallgerður–Bergþóra feud (servant killings)
killings.avenger_relation: member of Njáll's household (freedman's son, foster of the Njálssons) (ch.39)
killings.evidence: ch.38: "Bergþóra mun þér því heita sem hún mun efna að fyrir þig munu komu mannhefndir." ch.39: "Þú skalt fara ... og drepa Brynjólf frænda Hallgerðar."

killings.feud_name: Hallgerður–Bergþóra feud (servant killings)
killings.avenger_relation: Gunnar's kinsman living at Hlíðarendi, acting for Hallgerður (ch.41)
killings.evidence: ch.41: "Eigi er gott við að una við það hundrað silfurs er þú tókst fyrir Brynjólf frænda minn enda skal eg hefna hans láta ef eg má"

killings.feud_name: Hallgerður–Bergþóra feud (servant killings)
killings.avenger_relation: Sigmundur's companion staying at Hlíðarendi, acting for Hallgerður (ch.41)
killings.evidence: ch.41: "Því hafið þið heitið félagar Sigmundur og Skjöldur að drepa Þórð leysingjason fóstra Njálssona"
killings.note: Joint killing with KL011 (Sigmundur gave the death thrust).

killings.feud_name: Hallgerður–Bergþóra feud (servant killings)
killings.evidence: ch.45: "Tak vopn þín og ver þig. Er það nú meiri nauðsyn en kveða flím um oss bræður." ch.43: "þá munum vér minnast á hinn forna fjandskap."
killings.settled_after: yes (ch.45, Gunnar awards 200 silver, Skjöldur unatoned)
killings.note: Immediate trigger is Sigmundur's níð verses (ch.44); link to Þórður's killing rests on Þórður's prophecy "Skarphéðinn mun mín hefna" (ch.42) and Skarphéðinn's "forna fjandskap" (ch.43). Skjöldur (killed by Grímur and Helgi) is not in the list.

killings.evidence: ch.82: "Þessi tíðindi spurði Hákon jarl og lét dæma Kol útlagan um allt ríki sitt og lagði fé til höfuðs honum."

killings.feud_name: Killing of Höskuldur Hvítanesgoði and the Burning of Njáll
killings.evidence: ch.155: Kári: "Það munu margir mæla herra að eg hafi þetta verk fyrir yður unnið að hefna hirðmanns yðvars."
killings.note: Helgi was Sigurður jarl's retainer (ch.153). Kári also said he would avenge his son Þórður (ch.147). Gunnar Lambason was a burner and had just told a slanted account of the burning. Kári stayed outside the ch.145 settlement.

killings.feud_name: Killing of Höskuldur Hvítanesgoði and the Burning of Njáll
killings.avenges_person: Þórður Kárason, Njáll and those burned
killings.avenger_relation: father of Þórður Kárason; son-in-law of Njáll (ch.90)
killings.evidence: ch.147: "sonar míns kalla eg vera óhefnt og ætla eg mér einum það að hefna hans"; ch.158: "hann lést enn á þeim hafa óhefnt harma sinna."
killings.note: Kolur Þorsteinsson was a burner who mocked the most. Main stated motive is his son Þórður (blood), whose death is not a separate kid; relation_category is coded for Njáll (KL052), the avenged kid.

feuds.feud_name: Killing of Þorvaldur Ósvífsson (Hallgerður's first marriage)
feuds.summary: Þorvaldur slaps Hallgerður; her foster-father Þjóstólfur avenges the blow by killing him. Ósvífur claims son-compensation and Hrútur awards 200 silver (ch.12).
After a quarrel Þjóstólfur kills Glúmur; Hrútur then kills Þjóstólfur. Glúmur's brother Þórarinn is given gifts in lieu of compensation (ch.17).
Genealogical aside: Ásgrímur became the slayer of his foster-brother Gaukur; no details given.

After the seating insult (ch.35) the two housewives have each other's servants and kinsmen killed in turn: Svartur, Kolur, Atli, Brynjólfur, Þórður leysingjason, Sigmundur. Gunnar and Njáll settle each killing; ends with Gunnar's award for Sigmundur (ch.45).

feuds.feud_name: Gunnar of Hlíðarendi vs. Otkell, Starkaður and their allies
sides: Gunnar's opponents (Otkell, Starkaður, Geir goði, Mörður)
feuds.summary: From the Kirkjubær theft and the spur-blow, through the horse-fight ambush at Knafahólar and the ambush by the two Þorgeirs, Gunnar kills repeatedly, is outlawed and killed (ch.77); Högni and Skarphéðinn avenge him (ch.79), and settlements follow (ch.80).

feuds.feud_name: Þráinn kills the outlaw viking Kolur
feuds.summary: Hákon jarl puts a price on the outlaw Kolur's head; Þráinn hunts him down in Denmark and brings his head to the earl.
Back-story: Hrappur has killed Örlygur in Iceland and flees abroad; Vopnfirðingar are entitled to prosecute.

feuds.feud_name: Hrappur affair in Norway (Hákon jarl vs. Hrappur and the Njálssons)
feuds.summary: Hrappur seduces Guðbrandur's daughter and kills his overseer, is outlawed and escapes with Þráinn; the earl turns on the Njálssons, who kill two of his men before Kári rescues them. The grievance passes to the Njálssons–Þráinn feud.
One-line aside about the man to whom Þráinn gave his ship.

The Njálssons, wronged in Norway over Hrappur and insulted at Grjótá, kill Þráinn (ch.92); his brother-in-law Lýtingur avenges him on Höskuldur Njálsson (ch.98), whose blind son Ámundi kills Lýtingur (ch.106); each is settled.

feuds.feud_name: Þangbrandur kills Þorkell in a duel
feuds.summary: Þorkell opposes the faith and challenges Þangbrandur to a duel, which Þangbrandur wins.
Veturliði speaks most against the new faith and is killed for it.
The berserk fails the fire-ordeal and is cut down by Þangbrandur and Guðleifur.

feuds.feud_name: Killing of Höskuldur Hvítanesgoði and the Burning of Njáll
feuds.summary: Incited by Mörður's slander, the Njálssons and Kári kill Höskuldur; Flosi, egged on by Hildigunnur, rejects the award and burns Njáll and his sons; the case ends in a battle at the Althing and a general settlement (ch.145), Kári keeps up his revenge abroad until he and Flosi are fully reconciled (ch.159).

feuds.feud_name: Kolbeinn and Egill kill Arnór Örnólfsson
feuds.summary: Back-story cited by Hildigunnur: Flosi's brothers killed Arnór at Skaftafellsþing for a minor wrong against their father.
Back-story in Skarphéðinn's taunt: after killing Ketill Skafti disguised himself and hid.
Back-story: Hallur of Síða got Flosi's kinsman Þorgrímur out of the country after he killed Halli rauði.
